# Rolling Hurst / variance ratio - report

**Slug:** `family-hurst-persistence`
**Window:** 2016-01-04 -> 2023-12-29, development only. The 2024-2026
holdout was never loaded. A separate process deposited `holdout.json` / `holdout_run.log` in this folder after the development run; this agent did not read or use them.
**Execution:** `research/bt.py`, 1-minute marks, next-open fills, 2% band,
long-only, weights >= 0, sum <= 1. Headline 1 bp; 5 bp and 10 bp also reported.
**Primary:** rolling Hurst of QQQ daily returns, W = 252, q = 5; expanding
30/70 percentile thresholds over the prior 1,260 estimates (minimum 60).
TQQQ 1.0 when H <= q30, or when q30 < H < q70 and the QQQ 5-day return is
positive; BIL otherwise.

---

## 1. Headline

| cost | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | vol | TQQQ exposure | fills | turnover |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **1 bp** | **53.13%** | **60.40%** | **1.17** | 1.64 | 45.7% | **46.6%** | 341 | 5,005x |
| 5 bp | 50.53% | 60.46% | 1.13 | 1.58 | 45.7% | 46.6% | 341 | 4,543x |
| 10 bp | 47.35% | 60.54% | 1.08 | 1.52 | 45.7% | 46.6% | 341 | 4,030x |

The stated bar is TQQQ **36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD / 0.82 Sharpe** on daily
closes. The local 1-minute `bt.benchmark` TQQQ is 36.15% / 82.29% / 0.80; the
0.57 pp difference is a mark-convention difference. The primary clears both at
1 bp, 5 bp and 10 bp.

Ending equity at 1 bp is **$3,002,942** from $100,000. The sleeve is in TQQQ
46.6% of bars and in BIL the other 53.4%.

Daily-return correlation to TQQQ is **0.679**. Correlation to the nine current
winners ranges from **0.346 to 0.621**. This is a timing overlay on leveraged
Nasdaq beta, not a diversifying alpha.

## 2. Benchmarks

| | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | Calmar | TQQQ exposure |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| primary 1 bp | 53.13% | 60.40% | 1.17 | 0.88 | 46.6% |
| TQQQ | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | 0.44 | 100% |
| QQQ | 18.91% | 37.30% | 0.90 | 0.51 | - |

## 3. Yearly returns and exposure

| year | strategy | TQQQ | TQQQ exposure | note |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 2016 | **0.1%** | +19.9% | 0.0% | structural Hurst warm-up; no signal |
| 2017 | +35.1% | +114.5% | 49.8% | first trades from late March 2017 |
| 2018 | **+37.8%** | -20.8% | 18.3% | high-H cash state avoids the Q4 bear |
| 2019 | +126.9% | +148.2% | 88.9% | low-H state stays long |
| 2020 | **+196.6%** | +104.1% | 96.8% | low-H crash state is fully long |
| 2021 | +58.6% | +81.1% | 69.8% | lags the melt-up |
| 2022 | **+7.4%** | -79.4% | 8.8% | high-H state is almost entirely cash |
| 2023 | +42.0% | +192.0% | 40.0% | lags the AI melt-up |

The strategy is a **defensive regime overlay**: it wins in 2018 and 2022 by
being out, lags the calm melt-ups of 2017, 2021 and 2023, and is fully
invested in the 2020 crash-recovery. The 2016 zero is a warm-up artefact: a
252-day estimator cannot produce a signal before 2017.

## 4. What the Hurst state actually contains

The estimate is uniformly below 0.5: mean **0.433**, min **0.287**, max
**0.511**, and only one day above 0.50. The original "H > 0.5 -> trend" leg is
therefore untestable in absolute terms.

| state | share of days | forward 20d TQQQ mean | forward 20d win |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| low H (<= q30) | 33.6% | positive | - |
| high H (>= q70) | 29.9% | **negative** | - |

The high-H state is not a trend-continuation state in QQQ; it is
disproportionately a persistent-downside / high-volatility state. The scan
that produced the rule found:

| scan variant | dev CAGR | dev max DD |
|---|---:|---:|
| always long in the top H tercile | **-8.8%** | 85.9% |
| high H + 5-day up -> long | **-11.8%** | 84.6% |
| low H + 5-day down -> long | +22.2% | 56.7% |
| low H always -> long | +32.0% | 64.1% |

The scan used full-sample thresholds, so these numbers illustrate the sign of
each leg, not the final expanding-threshold rule. The final 8-cell grid is in
section 6.

The low-H side is the tradable side. The primary keeps the low-H leg, adds the
neutral-band 5-day-up leg for exposure, and stays in cash in the high-H state.

## 5. Entries and episodes

85 entries / 85 closed episodes from 938 active days. The episode return is
the TQQQ open-to-open return from the first held session to the session after
the position is closed.

| statistic | value |
|---|---:|
| episodes | 85 |
| mean episode return | +5.81% |
| median | +1.38% |
| win rate | 56.5% |
| t-stat | 1.92 |
| bootstrap p(mean <= 0) | 0.0004 |
| bootstrap 95% CI | +1.49% .. +12.87% |
| worst / best | -11.94% / +243.7% |

The distribution is **strongly right-skewed**: one 2020 episode returns
+243.7%, while the median episode is only +1.4%. The bootstrap p is small but
the t-stat is 1.92; the positive mean is carried by a few crash-recovery
episodes, not by a uniform per-entry edge.

The entry-forward study (next open to the open 20 sessions later) gives:

| statistic | value |
|---|---:|
| n | 85 |
| mean | +5.00% |
| median | +7.59% |
| win | 67.1% |
| t | 3.21 |
| worst / best | -28.9% / +50.0% |

## 6. Pre-registered 8-cell grid

All at 1 bp, 1-minute marks. The primary is cell 1.

| # | W | q | band | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | TQQQ exp | fills |
|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | **252** | **5** | **30/70** | **53.13%** | **60.40%** | **1.17** | **46.6%** | 341 |
| 2 | 252 | 2 | 30/70 | 33.98% | 68.0% | 0.89 | 40.2% | 333 |
| 3 | 252 | 10 | 30/70 | 51.74% | **43.3%** | 1.20 | 43.1% | 273 |
| 4 | 126 | 5 | 30/70 | 54.70% | 65.8% | 1.17 | 49.4% | 389 |
| 5 | 126 | 2 | 30/70 | 36.96% | 70.4% | 0.94 | 45.2% | 357 |
| 6 | 126 | 10 | 30/70 | 27.44% | 57.0% | 0.76 | 50.8% | 357 |
| 7 | 252 | 5 | 25/75 | 47.22% | 65.5% | 1.07 | 47.5% | 365 |
| 8 | 252 | 5 | 35/65 | 52.28% | 64.1% | 1.17 | 45.3% | 249 |

**6 of 8 cells clear the bar.** The failures are W252/q2 (33.98%) and
W126/q10 (27.44%). The one-year window is the important choice: W=252/q=5 and
W=252/q=10 both pass, and W=126/q=5 passes. The q=10 cell at W=252 has a
materially better drawdown (43.3%) at a slightly lower CAGR, which is a useful
robustness check: the result is not specific to the 5-day VR horizon.

This is a plateau in the window dimension and in the quantile band, but not in
the VR horizon: q=2 fails at W=252 and q=10 fails at W=126. The report treats
those failures as genuine limitations, not as noise to be averaged away.

## 7. Subperiods and drawdown anatomy

| period | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | TQQQ exp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 41.12% | 27.6% | 1.43 | 39.1% |
| 2020-2021 | 120.73% | 60.4% | 1.42 | 83.3% |
| 2022-2023 | **23.72%** | 30.0% | 0.85 | 24.6% |
| ex-2020 | **34.25%** | 32.8% | 1.16 | 34.4% |
| ex-2022 | 52.39% | 60.4% | 1.17 | 45.5% |

The 2016-2019 cut is 41.1%, so the strategy is not only a 2020 trade. But
**ex-2020 is 34.25%, below the 36.72% TQQQ bar**, and the 2022-2023 cut is
23.7%. The full-window pass is helped materially by 2020. The honest summary
is: a defensive overlay with a real 2018/2022 drawdown benefit, whose return
premium over TQQQ depends on the 2020 crash-recovery.

**Worst drawdowns:**

| peak -> trough | depth | context |
|---|---:|---|
| 2020-02-20 -> 2020-03-23 | **-60.4%** | the COVID crash; the low-H state is fully long |
| 2020-09-03 -> 2020-09-21 | -38.3% | the September 2020 growth sell-off |
| 2021-02-17 -> 2021-03-05 | -32.8% | the February 2021 yield spike |

The maximum drawdown is in the 2020 crash, exactly the failure mode the
family predicts: the low-H state is the high-volatility crash state, and the
strategy is 96.8% invested in 2020.

## 8. Placebo

Two placebos, each 100 full 1-minute backtests:

| | mean CAGR | sd | p95 | max | p(real >= placebo) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| circular shift of the state | 18.8% | 10.9% | 35.9% | 45.2% | **0.00** |
| random permutation of the state | 15.1% | 13.4% | 37.1% | 44.5% | **0.00** |

The shift placebo preserves the state durations and the exact exposure; the
permutation preserves exposure but destroys clustering. The real 53.13% is
above the maximum of both 100-draw sets. The timing is distinguishable from
both placebos.

## 9. Correlation to the nine current winners

| winner | correlation |
|---|---:|
| relative-value-tqqq | 0.621 |
| family-short-reversal | 0.570 |
| family-rebalance-flow | 0.532 |
| ratio-froth | 0.493 |
| family-ml-microstructure | 0.492 |
| vol-scaled-crash-stop | 0.482 |
| family-session-timing | 0.461 |
| family-intraday-microstructure-day | 0.346 |
| fomc-opex-window | 0.346 |
| TQQQ | 0.679 |

All nine correlations are below 0.85; the maximum is 0.62. The Hurst state is
not a duplicate of any existing family. The stored winner curves were truncated at 2023-12-29 before any return was computed; no 2024-2026 value was inspected.

## 10. Causality and implementation

- `H[d]` uses QQQ close-to-close returns through the **15:59 ET** close. The
  target is written on that bar and fills at the **09:30 open** of the next
  session. No 16:00 print is used.
- Thresholds use only H estimates up to and including day d; the lookback is
  1,260 observations with a 60-observation minimum.
- Truncating the panel at the **2020-03-12 11:07** cut leaves **409,376**
  prior weights identical: `max_abs_weight_diff = 0.0`.
- No full-sample normalisation. No moving average, no volatility targeting,
  no drawdown/capitulation event, no calendar clock, no opening-range or
  close-flow, no relative strength, no ML.
- Long-only, weights are 0 or 1, sum <= 1, BIL is the flat asset. 2% band;
  341 fills; 1 bp headline plus 5/10 bp.
- The result is deterministic; the only randomness is the placebo, seeded at
  11.

## 11. Kill criteria - verdict

| # | criterion | value | triggered? |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | 1 bp CAGR <= 36.72% or DD >= 82.29% | 53.13% / 60.40% | no |
| 2 | fewer than 5/8 grid cells pass | 6/8 | no |
| 3 | 10 bp CAGR <= 36.72% | 47.35% | no |
| 4 | shift-placebo p > 0.05 | 0.00 | no |
| 5 | shuffle-placebo p > 0.05 | 0.00 | no |
| 6 | ex-2020 CAGR <= 25% | 34.25% | no |
| 7 | correlation to a winner > 0.85 | 0.621 max | no |
| 8 | < 100 fills or < 30 entries | 341 / 85 | no |
| 9 | pre-cut max weight diff > 1e-12 | 0.0 | no |

**Verdict: dev pass, with a 2020-dependence caveat.** The primary clears the
TQQQ bar at 1/5/10 bp, 6/8 grid cells pass, both placebos reject at p = 0.00,
and the maximum winner correlation is 0.62. The caveats are real: 2016 is
cash (estimator warm-up), ex-2020 CAGR is 34.25% (below the TQQQ bar), and the
episode mean is carried by a handful of right-tail 2020-2021 entries. The
family is a useful defensive regime overlay, not a stand-alone replacement for
TQQQ.
hypothesis_md:
# Rolling Hurst / variance ratio - `family-hurst-persistence`

**Window:** 2016-01-04 -> 2023-12-29, development only. The 2024-2026
holdout is never loaded.

**Family:** persistence / mean-reversion regime estimated from the Hurst
exponent. The primary object is the Hurst estimate, not a moving average.

---

## 1. Mechanism

The Hurst exponent summarises how quickly the variance of a return series
scales with the horizon. For a random walk H = 0.5. H > 0.5 means increments
are positively autocorrelated (persistence / trend), H < 0.5 means they are
negatively autocorrelated (mean reversion).

The family hypothesis is:

- H > 0.5: trend continuation is favoured -> hold the long sleeve.
- H < 0.5: mean reversion is favoured -> buy declines.
- H ~ 0.5: no edge -> cash.

QQQ daily returns are negatively autocorrelated over 2016-2023. The rolling
estimate never reaches 0.5 in this sample: the full-dev mean is **0.433**, the
minimum **0.287**, the maximum **0.511**, and only one day is above 0.50. The
absolute version of the hypothesis therefore cannot be tested as written; the
test has to be whether the *relative* Hurst state separates forward returns.

A coarse development scan found that the low-H side is the risk-on side and
the high-H side is the risk-off side. The high-H state is not a trend-
continuation state in QQQ; it is disproportionately a persistent-downside /
high-volatility state. The primary rule keeps the low-H (mean-reversion) leg
and the neutral-band drift leg, and stands aside in the high-H state. This is
the inverse of the naive "persistent -> trend" reading, and the report states
it plainly rather than pretending the original sign worked.

## 2. Exact rules

### Estimation window

```
r[d]   = QQQ_close[d] / QQQ_close[d-1] - 1          (15:59 ET closes)
VR(q)  = Var(sum of q consecutive r) / (q * Var(r))  over the last W returns
H[d]   = 0.5 + log(VR(q)) / (2 * log(q))
W = 252, q = 5
```

`H[d]` uses only returns through the 15:59 close of day d. The thresholds are
the expanding 30th and 70th percentiles of the H estimates over a rolling
window of at most **1,260** observations (including the current estimate),
with a minimum of **60** estimates. The minimum is what lets the strategy start
in March 2017 rather than January 2018; it is causal and uses no future
observations.

The first H estimate needs 252 daily returns, so the first valid H is
**2017-01-03**. The first quantile threshold needs 60 H estimates, so the first
trade is **2017-03-29**. 2016 is therefore a structural cash year. That is a
real cost of a one-year estimator, not an intentional filter.

### Position rule (known at the 15:59 close of d; fill at the next 09:30 open)

```
if H[d] <= q30[d]:
    TQQQ 1.0                       # strong mean reversion: stay long
elif q30[d] < H[d] < q70[d] and QQQ_5d_return[d] > 0:
    TQQQ 1.0                       # neutral band, short-term drift up
else:
    BIL 1.0                        # high-H persistent state, or neutral-down
```

The 5-day return is only the direction selector inside the neutral band. It is
not a moving average, and it is not the regime variable.

### Execution

`research/bt.py`, 1-minute marks, next-open fills, 2% band, long-only,
weights >= 0, row sum <= 1. Headline cost 1 bp; 5 bp and 10 bp also reported.
BIL is the flat asset, so the cash return is the T-bill return.

## 3. Pre-registered 8-cell grid

The grid was fixed before the final run. It varies the estimator window, the
variance-ratio horizon and the quantile band; the rule is unchanged.

| # | W | q | band | role |
|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| 1 | **252** | **5** | **30/70** | **primary** |
| 2 | 252 | 2 | 30/70 | short VR horizon |
| 3 | 252 | 10 | 30/70 | long VR horizon |
| 4 | 126 | 5 | 30/70 | half-year window |
| 5 | 126 | 2 | 30/70 | half-year, short VR |
| 6 | 126 | 10 | 30/70 | half-year, long VR |
| 7 | 252 | 5 | 25/75 | wider tails |
| 8 | 252 | 5 | 35/65 | narrower core |

## 4. Falsifiers

The family is rejected, or downgraded to marginal, if any of these hold on
dev:

1. Primary 1 bp CAGR <= 36.72% or max drawdown >= 82.29%.
2. Fewer than 5 of the 8 grid cells clear the same bar.
3. 10 bp CAGR <= 36.72%.
4. Shift-placebo p > 0.05.
5. Shuffle-placebo p > 0.05.
6. Ex-2020 CAGR <= 25%.
7. Daily-return correlation to any of the nine current winners > 0.85.
8. Fewer than 100 fills or fewer than 30 independent entries.
9. Pre-cut max weight difference > 1e-12.

## 5. Expected failure modes

- **2020 crash:** the low-H state is exactly the high-volatility crash state,
  so the strategy is nearly fully invested into February-March 2020. The
  largest drawdown should be there, not in 2022.
- **2016-2017 cash drag:** the estimator needs a year of returns and three
  months of H history. The first two calendar years should be poor.
- **Right-skewed episode distribution:** a handful of low-H entries in 2020
  and 2021 carry a large share of the compounded return. The median episode
  should be much smaller than the mean.
- **High TQQQ correlation:** roughly half the time in TQQQ gives a daily
  correlation around 0.65-0.70. This is a timing overlay on leveraged Nasdaq
  beta, not a diversifying alpha.
- **Parameter sensitivity:** the 126-day/q=10 cell should be weak; the
  one-year/q=5 cell is the economic prior.

## 6. What this is not

- Not a 20/50/100/150/165/200-day moving-average trend gate: no moving
  average is computed.
- Not volatility targeting: the position is 0 or 1; there is no vol estimate
  in the sizing.
- Not a drawdown / capitulation event: no peak-to-trough state machine.
- Not a calendar clock: no FOMC, OpEx, turn-of-month or session-time rule.
- Not relative strength: no QQQ/SPY or TQQQ/QQQ ratio.
- Not opening-range or close-flow: the only intraday input is the 15:59 close.

## 7. Design provenance

The Hurst estimate and the quantile thresholds were computed on the
development window only. A coarse scan first tested the literal hypothesis
(high H -> long trend, low H -> fade), and the high-H long leg lost money
(always-long in the top H tercile: -8.8% dev CAGR; high-H + 5-day-up: -11.8%).
The low-H state was the profitable side. The rule above and the 8-cell grid
were then frozen, and the final run was made once. No 2024-2026 data was
loaded at any point. The inversion is reported as a finding, not hidden.

"""Rolling Hurst / variance ratio - `family-hurst-persistence`.

DEVELOPMENT WINDOW ONLY (2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29).  The 2024-2026 holdout is
never loaded.

Primary object
--------------
The rolling Hurst exponent estimated from the variance ratio of QQQ daily
close-to-close returns:

    VR(q) = Var(q-day return) / (q * Var(1-day return))
    H     = 0.5 + log(VR(q)) / (2 * log(q))

with W = 252 daily returns and q = 5.  H < 0.5 is the mean-reverting side of
the family hypothesis; H > 0.5 is the persistent side.  QQQ's daily returns are
negatively autocorrelated over this sample, so the estimate is centred near
0.43-0.45, not 0.50.  The strategy therefore uses the *relative* Hurst state:
the expanding 30th and 70th percentiles of the prior 1,260 daily estimates
(minimum 60 estimates).

Rule (known at the 15:59 close of day d; fills at the next 09:30 open):
    H[d] <= q30[d]                  -> TQQQ 1.0   (strong mean reversion)
    q30 < H[d] < q70 and 5d ret > 0 -> TQQQ 1.0   (neutral, short-term drift up)
    otherwise                       -> BIL 1.0

No moving average is used.  The 5-day return is only the direction selector
inside the neutral Hurst band; the regime itself is the Hurst estimate.

Run:
    $env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\\Users\\27175\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\opencode\\pylibs"
    $env:BT_THREADS = "1"
    python research/strategies/family-hurst-persistence/strategy.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "research"))
import bt  # noqa: E402

DEV_START, DEV_END = "2016-01-04", "2023-12-29"
BARS_PER_YEAR = 252 * 390
WARM = 20
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SLUG = "family-hurst-persistence"

PARAMS = dict(window=252, q=5, qlo=0.30, qhi=0.70, min_obs=60, look=1260)

WINNERS = [
    "ratio-froth", "vol-scaled-crash-stop", "relative-value-tqqq",
    "fomc-opex-window", "family-session-timing", "family-short-reversal",
    "family-rebalance-flow", "family-intraday-microstructure-day",
    "family-ml-microstructure",
]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# daily features
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def daily_features(ts, o, c):
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    nd = len(first)
    qc = c[last, 0]
    r1 = np.r_[np.nan, qc[1:] / qc[:-1] - 1.0]
    m5 = pd.Series(qc).pct_change(5).to_numpy()
    return dict(dates=dates, sess_dates=dates[first], first=first, last=last,
                nd=nd, qc=qc, r1=r1, m5=m5,
                tq=c[last, 1], tqo=o[first, 1], bil=c[last, 2])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hurst / variance ratio
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def hurst_series(ret, W, q):
    n = len(ret)
    out = np.full(n, np.nan)
    for i in range(W, n):
        x = ret[i - W + 1:i + 1]
        if not np.isfinite(x).all():
            continue
        v1 = float(np.var(x, ddof=0))
        if v1 <= 0:
            continue
        xq = np.convolve(x, np.ones(q), "valid")
        vq = float(np.var(xq, ddof=0))
        if vq <= 0:
            continue
        out[i] = 0.5 + np.log(vq / (q * v1)) / (2.0 * np.log(q))
    return out


def rolling_quantile(x, q, min_obs, look):
    n = len(x)
    out = np.full(n, np.nan)
    for i in range(n):
        v = x[max(0, i - look):i + 1]
        v = v[np.isfinite(v)]
        if len(v) >= min_obs:
            out[i] = float(np.quantile(v, q))
    return out


def hurst_state(f, params):
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    h = hurst_series(f["r1"], int(p["window"]), int(p["q"]))
    lo = rolling_quantile(h, float(p["qlo"]), int(p["min_obs"]), int(p["look"]))
    hi = rolling_quantile(h, float(p["qhi"]), int(p["min_obs"]), int(p["look"]))
    pos = np.where(h <= lo, 1.0,
                   np.where((h < hi) & (f["m5"] > 0), 1.0, 0.0))
    pos[~np.isfinite(h) | ~np.isfinite(lo) | ~np.isfinite(hi)] = 0.0
    pos[:WARM] = 0.0
    return pos, h, lo, hi


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# weights and episodes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def weights_from_pos(ts, f, pos):
    n = len(ts)
    w = np.zeros((n, 3))
    w[:, 2] = 1.0
    prev = 0.0
    for d in range(f["nd"]):
        target = float(pos[d])
        a, b = int(f["first"][d]), int(f["last"][d])
        w[a:b + 1, 1] = prev
        w[a:b + 1, 2] = 1.0 - prev
        w[b, 1] = target
        w[b, 2] = 1.0 - target
        prev = target
    return w


def episodes(f, pos):
    runs = []
    d = 0
    nd = f["nd"]
    while d < nd:
        if pos[d] <= 0:
            d += 1
            continue
        s = d
        while d < nd and pos[d] > 0:
            d += 1
        e = d - 1
        en = s + 1
        ex = min(e + 2, nd - 1)
        if en >= nd:
            continue
        runs.append((s, e, float(f["tqo"][en]), float(f["tqo"][ex])))
    return runs


def episode_stats(runs):
    rs = np.array([b / a - 1.0 for _, _, a, b in runs if a > 0 and b > 0])
    if len(rs) < 3:
        return {"n": int(len(rs))}
    t = float(rs.mean() / rs.std(ddof=1) * np.sqrt(len(rs))) if rs.std(ddof=1) > 0 else None
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    boot = rng.choice(rs, (10000, len(rs)), replace=True).mean(axis=1)
    return {"n": int(len(rs)), "mean": float(rs.mean()),
            "median": float(np.median(rs)), "win": float((rs > 0).mean()),
            "t": t, "bootstrap_p": float((boot <= 0).mean()),
            "ci95_low": float(np.quantile(boot, 0.025)),
            "ci95_high": float(np.quantile(boot, 0.975)),
            "worst": float(rs.min()), "best": float(rs.max())}


def build_weights(ts, o, c, params=None):
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    f = daily_features(ts, o, c)
    pos, h, lo, hi = hurst_state(f, p)
    w = weights_from_pos(ts, f, pos)
    runs = episodes(f, pos)
    entries = np.flatnonzero((pos > 0) & (np.r_[0.0, pos[:-1]] == 0))
    info = dict(params=p, signal_days=int((pos > 0).sum()),
                entries=int(len(entries)), episodes=len(runs),
                tqqq_exposure=float(np.mean(w[:, 1])),
                h_mean=float(np.nanmean(h)), h_min=float(np.nanmin(h)),
                h_max=float(np.nanmax(h)),
                frac_low=float(np.nanmean(np.where(np.isfinite(h), (h <= lo), np.nan))),
                frac_high=float(np.nanmean(np.where(np.isfinite(h), (h >= hi), np.nan))),
                episode_stats=episode_stats(runs))
    return w, info


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# evaluation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def metrics(pos, slip=1.0, start=DEV_START, end=DEV_END, w=None):
    if w is None:
        w = weights_from_pos(TS, F, pos)
    if start == DEV_START and end == DEV_END:
        r = bt.run(TS, O, C, w, start, band=0.02, slippage_bps=slip)
        s = bt.stats(r, BARS_PER_YEAR)
        ww = w
    else:
        i = bt.start_index(TS, start)
        j = int(TS.searchsorted(pd.Timestamp(end, tz="America/New_York"), side="right"))
        r = bt.simulate(TS[i:j], O[i:j], C[i:j], w[i:j], band=0.02,
                        slippage_bps=slip)
        s = bt.stats(r, BARS_PER_YEAR)
        ww = w[i:j]
    return {"cagr": s["cagr"], "max_drawdown": s["max_drawdown"],
            "sharpe": s["sharpe"], "sortino": s["sortino"],
            "volatility": s["volatility"], "fills": s["fills"],
            "turnover": s["turnover"], "ending_equity": s["ending_equity"],
            "tqqq_exposure": float(np.mean(ww[:, 1]))}


def daily_returns(pos, slip=1.0):
    r = bt.run(TS, O, C, weights_from_pos(TS, F, pos), DEV_START,
               band=0.02, slippage_bps=slip)
    eq = pd.Series(r["equity"], index=r["ts"])
    return eq.groupby(eq.index.date).last().pct_change().dropna()


def load_winner_returns(slug):
    path = ROOT / "research" / "new" / "curves" / f"{slug}.json"
    d = json.loads(path.read_text())
    dates = pd.to_datetime(d["dates"])
    keep = dates <= pd.Timestamp(DEV_END)
    vals = np.asarray(d["values"], dtype=float)[keep]
    return pd.Series(vals, index=dates[keep]).pct_change().dropna()


def correlations(pos):
    sr = daily_returns(pos)
    sr.index = pd.to_datetime(sr.index)
    out = {}
    for slug in WINNERS:
        wr = load_winner_returns(slug)
        j = sr.index.intersection(wr.index)
        out[slug] = float(np.corrcoef(sr.loc[j], wr.loc[j])[0, 1])
    tq = pd.Series(F["tq"], index=pd.to_datetime(F["sess_dates"]))
    tr = tq.pct_change().dropna()
    j = sr.index.intersection(tr.index)
    out["TQQQ"] = float(np.corrcoef(sr.loc[j], tr.loc[j])[0, 1])
    return out


def placebo(pos, n_draw=100, seed=11):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    real = metrics(pos)["cagr"]
    seg = pos[WARM:]
    shift_c, shuffle_c = [], []
    for _ in range(n_draw):
        sh = int(rng.integers(20, len(seg) - 20))
        q = np.r_[np.zeros(WARM), np.roll(seg, sh)]
        shift_c.append(metrics(q)["cagr"])
        q2 = np.r_[np.zeros(WARM), rng.permutation(seg)]
        shuffle_c.append(metrics(q2)["cagr"])

    def summ(v):
        a = np.asarray(v)
        return {"n_draws": int(len(a)), "mean_cagr": float(a.mean()),
                "std_cagr": float(a.std(ddof=1)),
                "p95_cagr": float(np.quantile(a, 0.95)),
                "max_cagr": float(a.max()),
                "p_value": float((a >= real).mean())}

    s = summ(shift_c)
    s["note"] = "circular shift of the daily state vector; preserves durations and exposure."
    r = summ(shuffle_c)
    r["note"] = "random permutation of the daily state vector; preserves exposure, destroys clustering."
    return {"real_cagr": real, "active_days": int((pos > 0).sum()),
            "shift": s, "shuffle": r}


def precut_check():
    cut = bt.start_index(TS, "2020-03-12")
    f = daily_features(TS[:cut], O[:cut], C[:cut])
    pos_cut, _, _, _ = hurst_state(f, PARAMS)
    w_cut = weights_from_pos(TS[:cut], f, pos_cut)
    w_full = weights_from_pos(TS, F, F["pos"])
    pre = min(len(w_cut), cut)
    return {"cut": "2020-03-12 11:07 America/New_York",
            "bars_compared": int(pre),
            "max_abs_weight_diff": float(np.max(np.abs(
                w_cut[:pre, 1] - w_full[:pre, 1])))}

    cells = [

    print("wrote", OUT / "result.json")


def _entry_forward(f, entries, hold):
    rs = []
    nd = f["nd"]
    for d in entries:
        en = d + 1
        ex = min(d + 1 + hold, nd - 1)
        if en >= nd:
            continue
        rs.append(float(f["tqo"][ex] / f["tqo"][en] - 1.0))
    rs = np.asarray(rs, dtype=float)
    if len(rs) < 3:
        return {"n": int(len(rs))}
    t = float(rs.mean() / rs.std(ddof=1) * np.sqrt(len(rs))) if rs.std(ddof=1) > 0 else None
    return {"n": int(len(rs)), "mean": float(rs.mean()),
            "median": float(np.median(rs)), "win": float((rs > 0).mean()),
            "t": t, "worst": float(rs.min()), "best": float(rs.max())}
